S40.01.note: The server prompt says to use the preferred name sparingly and never to open a reply (apps/web/lib/server/user-identity.ts:184), so the name may not appear in every reply. The Settings menu item text is confirmed in AccountFooter.tsx; the trigger that opens that menu was not confirmed in the code.
steps: Sign in, open the account menu and choose Settings, then click Personalization.
Scroll to About you and click the field under What should AGI call you?.
Type a nickname or first name you choose (the field holds up to 60 characters).
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a short greeting, and check whether the reply uses the name.
S40.01.where: Settings > Personalization > About you > What should AGI call you?

steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
In About you, click the box under More about you and type a background detail, such as a hobby or a field you work in.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat and ask a question where that background would matter.
Compare the reply with Expected. The box holds up to 1,500 characters.
S40.02.where: Settings > Personalization > About you > More about you

S40.03.note: The role list comes from apps/web/features/settings/constants/work-descriptions.ts, which was not opened in detail.
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
In About you, open the list under What best describes your work? and pick a role.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat and ask for help with a task that fits the role you picked.
Compare the reply with Expected.
S40.03.where: Settings > Personalization > About you > What best describes your work?

S40.05.note: The composer Style button has the same five presets and works per conversation (see S40.19).
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Response style and pick Explanatory.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a chat and click the Style button in the composer to confirm it shows the same choice.
Send a question and compare the reply with Expected.

S40.06.note: The composer Style menu also has a Response Length row with Brief, Default and Thorough (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/StyleSelector.tsx).
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Response length and pick Shorter.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, ask a question that has a long answer, and compare its length with Expected.

S40.07.note: No separate formality control was found. The closest is the Formal preset (described as Formal register in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/StyleSelector.tsx:35), so there is no less-formal setting other than Default.
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Response style and pick Formal.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a casual question, and compare the register of the reply with Expected.

S40.08.note: The named presets are Default, Concise, Explanatory, Learning and Formal. Warmth, Enthusiasm, Headers and lists and Emoji are separate settings (S40.09 to S40.12).
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Response style and pick Learning.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a question, and compare the reply with Expected.
Change to Concise and send the same question, then compare again.

S40.09.note: The trait options are Less, Default and More.
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open the list under Warmth.
Pick More, then wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a question, and compare the warmth of the reply with Expected.
Pick Less, send the same question, and compare again.
Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open the list under Enthusiasm.
Pick Less, then wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a question, and compare the enthusiasm of the reply with Expected.
Pick More, send the same question, and compare again.

S40.11.note: Two controls cover this: Preferred formatting (Not set, Prose, Bullet lists, Headings and bullets, Tables and code) and the Headers and lists trait.
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Preferred formatting and pick Prose.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, ask a question that could have a list, and check whether the reply is prose or uses lists.
Compare with Expected. Headers and lists can also be turned Less or More under Characteristics.
Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Scroll to Characteristics and open the list under Emoji.
Pick Less, then wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a question that invites emoji, and check whether the reply uses any.
Pick More, send the same question, and compare with Expected.
Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Technical level and pick Beginner.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, ask a technical question, and compare the depth of the reply with Expected.
Pick Expert, ask the same question again, and compare.

S40.14.note: This is separate from Display Language under Settings > General (apps/web/features/settings/sections/GeneralSection.tsx).
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Open the list under Response language and pick a language other than Match my message, such as French.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, write a message in English, and check which language the reply uses.
Compare with Expected.

S40.16.note: The switch has no visible text; its accessible name is Apply instructions for AGI in the same file. When off, the hint reads Off. Your instructions are kept and not sent to the model.
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Click the box under Instructions for AGI and type a standing rule, such as always end with a one-line summary.
Wait for the Saved text under the Personalization heading.
Open a new chat, send a question, and check that the reply follows the rule.
Turn off the switch beside Instructions for AGI, open a new chat, send the same question, and check the rule is no longer followed while the text stays in the box.

S40.17.note: The row menu label comes from packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx; the trigger that opens it was not separately confirmed.
steps: In the left sidebar, open the menu on a project row and click Project settings.
In the Instructions box, type a rule for that project, such as answer in short bullets.
Click Save.
Open a chat inside that project, send a question, and check the reply follows the rule.
Open a chat in a different project and check it does not follow the same rule.
S40.17.where: Sidebar > your project's row menu > Project settings > Instructions

S40.19.note: The composer choice is stored per conversation in apps/web/features/chat/stores/style-store.ts; the Personalization default is a separate setting.
steps: Open a chat that already has messages and click the Style button in the composer.
Click Concise and send a message.
Compare the reply with Expected.
Open a second chat and check its Style button still shows its own choice.
Open Settings > Personalization > Response style and check the default there did not change.
S40.19.where: Style > Concise (composer, in an open chat)

S40.20.needs: a writing sample of your own
S40.20.note: The sample box exists only in the composer custom style form, not in Settings. The instruction is auto-filled only when it is empty and the sample is over 20 characters.
steps: Click the Style button in the composer, then click Create Custom Style.
Type a name, paste two or three sentences of your own writing into Writing sample, and check the Style instruction box fills in.
Click Save.
Send a message in that chat and compare the reply's tone with your sample.
Edit the style and check the sample is still there.
S40.20.where: Style > Create Custom Style > Writing sample

S40.23.note: The reset also clears the composer Style choice and per-conversation picks (apps/web/features/chat/stores/style-store.ts:225). It does not change custom styles or the instructions box.
steps: Open Settings, then click Personalization.
Change Response style to Concise and set one Characteristics trait to More.
Click Reset response style.
Check the toast text Response style is back to the defaults. and that Response style and the traits show Default.
Check that About you and Instructions for AGI kept their text.

S40.24.note: The same preset is also at Settings > Personalization > Response style.
steps: Open a chat and click the Style button in the composer.
Click Explanatory and send a question.
Compare the reply with Expected, looking for reasoning and context.
S40.24.where: Style > Explanatory (composer, in an open chat)

S40.25.note: The learning guidance is sent to the model from apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts; whether replies follow it was not judged.
steps: Open a chat and click the Style button in the composer.
Click Learning, which is described as Step by step, with check-ins, and send a question.
Compare the reply with Expected: teaching, quizzing and step-by-step structure.
S40.25.where: Style > Learning (composer, in an open chat)

steps: Open a chat and click the Style button in the composer.
Click Concise and send a question that normally gets a long answer.
Compare the reply with Expected: it should be short and direct.
S40.26.where: Style > Concise (composer, in an open chat)

S40.27.note: Deleting asks first, per the confirmation text, and removes the style on every device.
steps: Click the Style button in the composer, then click Create Custom Style.
Type a Name, a Style instruction such as Answer in two sentences, and click Save.
Check the new style is listed and selected. Click the pencil icon to edit it, change the name, and click Save changes.
Click the trash icon, then Delete style in the confirmation to delete it.
Check it is gone from the list and that the dialog warned it cannot be recovered.

labels.text: Use your profile and instructions for AGI

S40.30.needs: a project you own and a saved Instructions for AGI
S40.30.note: The box is ticked by default. The server choice is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts.
steps: In the left sidebar, open the menu on a project row and click Project settings.
Under Personalization, untick Use your profile and instructions for AGI and read the line beneath it.
Click Save.
Open a chat in that project and send a question, then compare with Expected.
Open a chat in another project that still has the box ticked and compare.
S40.30.where: Sidebar > your project's row menu > Project settings > Personalization
